narrative_passages.title: Ibrahim leaves idols
narrative_passages.treatment_reason: Ibrahim is never shown; his word to his people is read at the edge of town.

summary_for_children: Az-Zukhruf means Gold Ornaments. It reminds us that Allah made the earth a bed for us with roads, sends rain in measure, and gave us ships and animals to ride, and that gold and silver are small next to faith.
world_title: Roads Across the Bed of Earth
environment_concept: Roads across the earth (43:10), rain in measure reviving dead land (43:11), and ships and animals to ride (43:12).
architecture_and_scenery: Valleys with clear roads, ships and riding animals, and a gilded palace with silver roofs as a warning about worldly ornament.

palette.lighting: Clear daylight; a glittering palace that dims

unique_world.visual_theme: A bright street lined with silver and gold on a showcase terrace, a plain shed, a garden bed, a dark oak path, a shelter and a seed store

primary_mechanic.text: Pick up a thing and bring it to one of four needs (a dry garden, a dark path, a cold shelter, an empty seed store). Silver and gold are refused (43:33-35: only the enjoyment of worldly life); each need is met only by the plain thing that helps.

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading, the four needs around the street, then Ibrahim’s word and the roads
world_assets: water jar, lamp, blanket, seed sack
environment_behaviour: the carried thing is held in front of the explorer
a met need’s sign turns green and the useful thing stays there
unique_world.learning_objective: Understand that ornaments are only the enjoyment of this world (43:33-35)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The City of Gold
story_library.children_narration: Imagine a city filled with beautiful ornaments, golden decorations, and impressive buildings. Does having all those things make someone good or wise? Surah Az-Zukhruf reminds us that wealth and beauty are not the true measure of a person's worth. It also recalls the stories of Musa and Isa.

world_idea.title: The Golden City
world_idea.description: Explore an ornate city and learn to distinguish luxury from kindness, honesty, and sincere faith through interactive choices.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
